mental_models.name: Chesterton's Fence
mental_models.hint: Never remove a fence, rule, or piece of code until you understand why it was built in the first place.

mental_models.name: Inversion (Stoic / Jacobi)
mental_models.hint: Instead of asking how to succeed, ask how to avoid obvious failure and invert the problem.

mental_models.name: Second-Order Thinking
mental_models.hint: Always ask: 'And then what?' considering the downstream secondary and tertiary consequences.

mental_models.name: First Principles Thinking
mental_models.hint: Boil a problem down to its fundamental truths and reason up from there rather than by analogy.

mental_models.name: Gall's Law
mental_models.hint: All complex systems that work evolved from simple systems that worked. Designing complex systems from scratch always fails.

mental_models.name: Lindy Effect
mental_models.hint: The future life expectancy of non-perishable ideas/tools is proportional to their current age.

mental_models.name: Hanlon's Razor
mental_models.hint: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by carelessness or misunderstanding.

mental_models.name: Goodhart's Law
mental_models.hint: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.

mental_models.name: Occam's Razor
mental_models.hint: Among competing hypotheses, the one with the fewest assumptions is usually the correct one.

mental_models.name: Circle of Competence
mental_models.hint: Knowing the precise boundary of what you truly understand versus what you only think you understand.

mental_models.name: Conway's Law
mental_models.hint: Organizations design software architectures that mirror their internal communication structures.

mental_models.name: Parkinson's Law
mental_models.hint: Work expands so as to fill the time available for its completion.

mental_models.name: The Map is Not the Territory
mental_models.hint: Models, abstractions, and specs are useful representations, not reality itself.

mental_models.name: The Cobra Effect
mental_models.hint: When an attempted solution makes the original problem worse through perverse incentives.

cognitive_biases.name: Survivorship Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Focusing on visible winners while overlooking the invisible graveyard of failures.

cognitive_biases.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
cognitive_biases.hint: Continuing a failing project because you've already invested time, money, or effort.

cognitive_biases.name: Anchoring Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Relying too heavily on the first piece of information encountered when making decisions.

cognitive_biases.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: People with low expertise overestimating their ability, while experts underestimate theirs.

cognitive_biases.name: Fundamental Attribution Error
cognitive_biases.hint: Blaming others' actions on character flaws while excusing your own as situational.

cognitive_biases.name: Framing Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Drawing different conclusions from the exact same data depending on how it is presented.

cognitive_biases.name: Confirmation Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Searching for and interpreting information in a way that confirms preexisting beliefs.

cognitive_biases.name: Status Quo Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Preferring the current state of affairs over change, even when change offers clear upside.

cognitive_biases.name: Curse of Knowledge
cognitive_biases.hint: Once you know something deeply, it is nearly impossible to imagine what it's like not to know it.

cognitive_biases.name: Peak-End Rule
cognitive_biases.hint: Judging an experience almost entirely based on how it felt at its peak and at its end.

paradoxes.name: Simpson's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A trend appears in several different groups of data but disappears or reverses when the groups are combined.

paradoxes.name: Braess's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Adding capacity to a network can sometimes slow down overall throughput when agents act selfishly.

paradoxes.name: The Monty Hall Problem
paradoxes.hint: Why switching doors doubles your chances of winning from 1/3 to 2/3 due to conditional probability.

paradoxes.name: The Birthday Paradox
paradoxes.hint: In a room of just 23 people, there is a 50% chance two share the exact same birthday.

paradoxes.name: The Fermi Paradox
paradoxes.hint: If the universe is so vast and ancient, where are all the extraterrestrial civilizations?

paradoxes.name: Ship of Theseus
paradoxes.hint: If all parts of an object are replaced over time, does fundamental identity persist?

paradoxes.name: Jevons Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Increases in efficiency in using a resource tend to increase the overall rate of consumption of that resource.

paradoxes.name: The Mpemba Effect
paradoxes.hint: Under specific thermodynamic conditions, warm water can freeze faster than cold water.

neuroscience.name: The Zeigarnik Effect
neuroscience.hint: Uncompleted tasks create cognitive tension, consuming working memory until resolved or noted down.

neuroscience.name: Ultradian Rhythms
neuroscience.hint: The brain's natural 90-minute cycle of peak alertness followed by a mandatory 20-minute recovery trough.

neuroscience.name: Default Mode Network & Shower Epiphanies
neuroscience.hint: Why the brain makes its greatest creative breakthroughs when you disengage from active focus.

neuroscience.name: Cognitive Load Theory
neuroscience.hint: How context switching and micro-interruptions exhaust working memory before real deep work begins.

neuroscience.name: Spaced Repetition & Ebbinghaus Curve
neuroscience.hint: Why reviewing information right before you're about to forget it locks it permanently in memory.

neuroscience.name: Dopamine Prediction Error
neuroscience.hint: How anticipation and unexpected rewards drive motivation far more than the actual outcome.

thought_experiments.name: The Experience Machine (Nozick)
thought_experiments.hint: If a supercomputer could give you any pleasurable experience for life, would you plug in permanently?

thought_experiments.name: Mary the Color Scientist (Jackson)
thought_experiments.hint: A neuroscientist knows every physical fact about color from a black-and-white room. When she sees red, does she learn anything new?

thought_experiments.name: The Chinese Room (Searle)
thought_experiments.hint: A person follows rulebooks to translate Chinese symbols without understanding a word. Does the system understand?

thought_experiments.name: The Invisible Gorilla
thought_experiments.hint: When focusing intensely on one task, the human brain systematically tunes out obvious anomalies in plain sight.

quotes.name: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.hint: Stoic wisdom on focusing only on what is within your control.

quotes.name: Seneca
quotes.hint: On time management, brevity of life, and avoiding needless anxiety.

quotes.name: Epictetus
quotes.hint: On freedom, perception, and reacting to adversity with equanimity.

quotes.name: Lao Tzu
quotes.hint: On simplicity, patience, flow, and effortless action (Wu Wei).

quotes.name: Aristotle
quotes.hint: On virtue ethics, habits, and excellence as repeated practice.

quotes.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.hint: On overcoming adversity, self-mastery, and questioning defaults.

quotes.name: Confucius
quotes.hint: On continuous self-improvement, humility, and moral integrity.

quotes.name: Alan Watts
quotes.hint: On presence, Eastern philosophy, and letting go of rigid control.

quotes.name: Viktor Frankl
quotes.hint: On finding purpose in suffering and the space between stimulus and response.

quotes.name: Carl Jung
quotes.hint: On shadow work, self-awareness, and bringing the unconscious to light.

facts.name: Deep-Ocean Hydrothermal Vents
facts.hint: Ecosystems thriving in total darkness on chemosynthesis rather than sunlight.

facts.name: Fungal Mycorrhizal Networks
facts.hint: Underground fungal superhighways enabling trees and plants to trade nutrients and warnings.

facts.name: Superfluidity at Macro Scales
facts.hint: Liquid helium climbing container walls with zero viscosity near absolute zero.

facts.name: Corvid Tool Use & Problem Solving
facts.hint: Crows and ravens inventing multi-stage tools and passing knowledge down generations.

facts.name: Polynesian Open-Ocean Star Navigation
facts.hint: Navigating thousands of miles of open Pacific using swell patterns, birds, and star paths.

facts.name: Ant Colony Decentralized Computing
facts.hint: Ant colonies solving complex traveling-salesman routing problems with zero central coordination.
